_about: The weather a day at the range is drawn from, by course, by month and by time of day (morning, midday, afternoon). Each course has twelve months, each with the mean daily low and high (F), the mean relative humidity, the mean wind (mph) and the chance of a Santa Ana day. A time of day puts the temperature between the low and the high (tempAt), scales the wind (windFactor) and shifts the humidity; dayToDaySpreadF is the day-to-day scatter around the month's figure. The wind is drawn in three stretches of the path that differ from one another, each with a gust, and always has some crosswind. A Santa Ana day replaces the wind, the humidity and part of the temperature.

tempAt.estimate: where between the month's mean low and mean high the temperature sits: a morning at the range (soon after opening, 8 to 10 am) is near the day's low, which comes just before sunrise, and has begun to climb

windFactor.estimate: the wind at this time of day as a share of the day's mean: in these inland valleys the sea breeze "build[s] during daylight hours, typically peaking in the late afternoon when inland heating is at its peak" (https://gotbooks.miracosta.edu/fieldtrips/weather/weather.html) and the land breeze of the night is light, so a morning runs at about half the daily mean, midday about the mean, and an afternoon about half again as much; not a measured hourly climatology, which neither site publishes

humidityShift.estimate: relative humidity is highest in the cool of the morning and lowest in the heat of the afternoon; about 15 points above the daily mean in the morning and 15 below in the afternoon, the usual swing for a dry inland day; not measured for these sites

tempAt.estimate: late morning to early afternoon, 11 am to 1 pm: most of the way from the low to the high

windFactor.estimate: the same basis as the morning's factor in this file: about the daily mean

humidityShift.estimate: the same basis as the morning's shift in this file: about the daily mean

tempAt.estimate: mid afternoon, 2 to 4 pm: at or near the day's high

windFactor.estimate: the same basis as the morning's factor in this file: the sea breeze's late-afternoon peak, about half again the daily mean

humidityShift.estimate: the same basis as the morning's shift in this file: about 15 points below the daily mean

dayToDaySpreadF.estimate: a day at the range is not the month's average day: the temperature is drawn within plus or minus 6 F of the month's figure for that time of day (uniformly). The day-to-day standard deviation of daily highs in Southern California runs about 5 to 7 F; not computed from these sites' records

low.estimate: a day's wind is drawn between half and 1.6 times the month's mean for that time of day: calm days and breezy days both happen; the band is an estimate around the mean, not a measured distribution

high.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

low.estimate: the gust on top of the steady wind, as a share of it: 20 to 50 percent, the usual gust factor of a light to moderate breeze over rough brushy ground; not measured at these ranges

high.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

low.estimate: gusts come and go over several seconds

high.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

stretchVariation.estimate: the three stretches of the path differ from the day's wind by up to 35 percent, and the far stretch (up the slope at Piru) is the most different

windFromDegrees.estimate: the wind comes from anywhere but straight down the range: between 20 and 160 degrees (from the right-hand side, clockwise from downrange) or 200 to 340 (from the left), so there is always some crosswind

santaAna._about: A Santa Ana day: the dry offshore wind of the cooler months. Drawn with the month's chance; on such a day the wind, the humidity and the temperature below replace the month's figures, and the wind is strongest in the morning.

source.note: the National Weather Service's scale as the Santa Clarita station reports it: a weak Santa Ana event is 15 to 25 mph winds out of the northeast with gusts to 40 mph; a moderate one 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 50; a strong one 20 to 40 mph with gusts to 60. tempAboveNormalF.estimate: the same report had temperatures "in the mid 80s to lower 90s" in Santa Clarita in October, against the month's mean high of 81 F; a Santa Ana day runs about 10 F above the month's figure for that time of day

morning.estimate: Santa Ana winds "reach their maximum in the morning and decay to their minimum in the late afternoon" (Guzman-Morales et al. 2016, https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/2016GL067887): the morning carries 1.2 times the drawn speed, midday the drawn speed, the afternoon 0.7 of it

midday.estimate: the same basis as the morning's factor in this entry

afternoon.estimate: the same basis as the morning's factor in this entry

words._about: The one word the day is described with, by temperature in F: cold below the first figure, cool to the second, mild to the third, warm to the fourth, hot above it; "dry" is added when the humidity is below dryBelow.

coldBelowF.estimate: the words a shooter would use for the air; plain thresholds, not a measurement: cold under 45, cool 45 to 64, mild 65 to 74, warm 75 to 84, hot from 85

coolBelowF.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

mildBelowF.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

warmBelowF.estimate: same basis: the same basis as the figure next to it in this entry

dryBelow.estimate: air under 25 percent relative humidity is called dry; a plain threshold

santaAnaChance.estimate: the chance that a day drawn in this month is a Santa Ana day (the hot, dry offshore wind of the cooler months). Basis: Santa Ana events "occur at least twice per average month" from October to April, are most frequent in December, and the hourly index "reach[es] their maximum in the morning" (Guzman-Morales et al. 2016, Geophysical Research Letters, https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/2016GL067887); an event lasts about 1.5 days on average and there are 10 to 25 a year (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ana_winds, citing Raphael 2003); so about 3 days a month from October to April (a chance near 0.1), more in December and January, a rare September one, none from May to August
